title: Career Explorer: Unlock Your Future
description: You're trapped in a career counselling centre that's about to close! Navigate through 4 rooms, each representing a different career field. Solve puzzles, find clues, and discover what career suits you best -- before time runs out!
learning_objectives: Understand the core skills and qualifications required for careers in technology, design, healthcare, and business
Learn about India-specific career pathways, entrance exams, and premier institutions (IIT, AIIMS, NIFT, IIMs)
Develop the ability to evaluate which career field aligns with personal strengths and interests
Recognise the real-world responsibilities and ethical dimensions of different professions
Build awareness of emerging career opportunities in India's evolving job market

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: You start in The Tech Lab -- tap on clues like code snippets, company profiles, and career guides to read them
Use the information from clues to solve each room's career puzzle
Answer the puzzle question correctly to unlock the next room
Progress through The Tech Lab, The Design Studio, The Medical Wing, and The Entrepreneur's Office
Complete all four rooms before the 7-minute timer runs out to escape and unlock your career profile!
tips: Read every clue carefully -- later clues often build on earlier ones and contain critical puzzle details
Think about real-world career requirements, not just textbook definitions
Some clues are locked until you discover earlier clues in the same room -- explore methodically
Pay attention to India-specific details like exam names, institutions, and industry context

rooms.title: The Tech Lab
rooms.description: You enter a room filled with glowing monitors, tangled cables, and whiteboards covered in algorithms. This is the world of software engineering and IT. Examine the clues to understand what it really takes to build a career in tech -- then solve the puzzle to move on!

clues.label: Code on the Whiteboard
clues.content:
A whiteboard shows a problem and solution:

PROBLEM: Find the shortest path between two cities on a map.
SOLUTION APPROACH: Dijkstra's Algorithm

NOTE SCRIBBLED BELOW:
'Software engineering isn't just about writing code -- it's about solving problems efficiently. An algorithm that works on 100 users might crash with 1 million. That's why Big Tech companies (Google, Microsoft, Flipkart) test algorithmic thinking in interviews, not just coding syntax.'

TIME COMPLEXITY: O((V + E) log V)
clues.hint: This clue reveals what tech companies truly value in engineers. Is it memorising syntax, or understanding how to solve problems at scale?

clues.label: Tech Career Pathway Chart
clues.content:
CAREER PATHWAY: SOFTWARE ENGINEER IN INDIA

1. EDUCATION:
   - Class 11-12: PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Maths) stream
   - Entrance Exams: JEE Main/Advanced (for IITs), BITSAT, state CETs
   - Top Colleges: IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad, NIT Trichy
   - Degree: B.Tech/B.E. in Computer Science or IT (4 years)

2. KEY SKILLS BEYOND CODING:
   - Data Structures & Algorithms
   - System Design & Architecture
   - Version Control (Git)
   - Team collaboration & code reviews
   - Continuous learning (tech changes every 2-3 years)

3. STARTING SALARY RANGE:
   - Service companies (TCS, Infosys, Wipro): ₹3.5-6 LPA
   - Product companies (Google, Microsoft, Flipkart): ₹15-45 LPA
   - Startups: ₹8-20 LPA + equity
clues.hint: Notice the huge salary range. What do you think separates a ₹4 LPA role from a ₹40 LPA role? It comes back to problem-solving depth.

clues.label: Developer's Journal Entry
clues.content:
JOURNAL -- Day 247 at a Bangalore startup:

'Today I spent 3 hours debugging a payment gateway issue. The code was fine -- the problem was that I didn't understand the business logic properly. My manager said something that stuck with me: "The best engineers don't just code -- they understand WHY they're building something and WHO will use it."

I've started sitting in on product meetings now. Understanding user pain points has made me a 10x better developer than learning another framework ever could.

Note to self: Tech skills get you hired. Communication and business understanding get you promoted.'
clues.hint: This developer learned something crucial about what separates good engineers from great ones. It's not just technical skill.

clues.label: Tech Roles Poster
clues.content:
IT ISN'T JUST 'CODING' -- EXPLORE THESE TECH ROLES:

- Software Developer: Builds applications and systems
- Data Scientist: Analyses large datasets to find patterns (needs strong statistics + Python/R)
- Cybersecurity Analyst: Protects systems from hackers (CEH, OSCP certifications)
- DevOps Engineer: Bridges development and operations (cloud platforms like AWS, Azure)
- AI/ML Engineer: Builds intelligent systems (needs linear algebra, calculus, deep learning)
- Product Manager: Guides what to build and why (needs both tech understanding + business sense)

FUN FACT: India produces 1.5 million engineering graduates annually, but only 3-5% are considered industry-ready by top recruiters. The differentiator? Real projects, internships, and problem-solving ability.
clues.hint: Tech is a vast field with many specialisations. Not all of them require hardcore coding -- some need business sense, statistics, or security expertise.

puzzle.question: A Class 12 student passionate about technology wants to maximise their career potential in software engineering. Based on the clues, which combination of actions would be MOST effective?
options: Learn 10 programming languages, skip college, and apply directly to Google
Focus on JEE preparation for a top CS program, build algorithmic problem-solving skills, work on real projects, and develop communication abilities
Get any engineering degree, then join a service company -- the brand name of the college doesn't matter in tech
Skip the theory and algorithms -- just learn web development from YouTube tutorials and freelance
puzzle.correct_answer: Focus on JEE preparation for a top CS program, build algorithmic problem-solving skills, work on real projects, and develop communication abilities
puzzle.success_message: Excellent! You've cracked The Tech Lab! A strong foundation (top college + algorithms) combined with practical skills (projects) and soft skills (communication) is the winning formula in tech. You've unlocked The Design Studio!
puzzle.fail_message: Not quite! The clues showed that top tech careers need a combination: strong educational foundation, algorithmic thinking, real-world projects, AND communication skills. No single shortcut works. Try again!

rooms.title: The Design Studio
rooms.description: Colourful mood boards line the walls, mannequins wear experimental outfits, and a sleek iMac displays a UX prototype. This is the world of creative arts and design. Discover what it takes to turn creativity into a career!

clues.label: Design Principles Wall
clues.content:
THE 5 PRINCIPLES EVERY DESIGNER MUST KNOW:

1. CONTRAST: Make important elements stand out (light vs dark, big vs small)
2. ALIGNMENT: Nothing should look randomly placed -- every element needs a visual connection
3. REPETITION: Consistent colours, fonts, and styles create a unified look
4. PROXIMITY: Related items should be grouped together
5. HIERARCHY: Guide the viewer's eye -- what should they see FIRST, SECOND, THIRD?

SCRIBBLED NOTE: 'Design is NOT about making things pretty. It's about solving problems visually. A beautiful app that users can't navigate is a failed design. A simple app that users love? That's great UX.'

Remember: 'Good design is invisible. You only notice bad design.' -- Dieter Rams
clues.hint: These principles apply whether you're designing a poster, an app, a building, or a fashion collection. Design is fundamentally about communication and problem-solving.

clues.label: Portfolio Building Guide
clues.content:
HOW TO BUILD A DESIGN PORTFOLIO THAT GETS YOU HIRED:

IMPORTANT: In design careers, your portfolio matters MORE than your degree.

1. SHOW YOUR PROCESS, not just final results
   - Include sketches, wireframes, mood boards, iterations
   - Explain WHY you made each design decision

2. QUALITY OVER QUANTITY
   - 5-8 strong projects beat 30 mediocre ones
   - Each project should show a different skill

3. REAL PROJECTS > CLASS ASSIGNMENTS
   - Redesign a real app's confusing feature
   - Design for a local business or NGO
   - Enter competitions (e.g., Adobe Design Achievement Awards)

4. TOOLS TO LEARN:
   - UI/UX: Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch
   - Graphic Design: Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop
   - Motion: After Effects, Blender
   - Fashion: CLO 3D, Adobe Illustrator for patterns
clues.hint: Unlike tech where exam scores open doors, design careers rely heavily on what you can SHOW. Your portfolio is your real resume.

clues.label: Design Careers in India
clues.content:
DESIGN CAREER PATHWAYS IN INDIA:

1. FASHION DESIGN:
   - Entrance: NIFT Entrance Exam, NID DAT, UCEED
   - Top Colleges: NIFT Delhi, NID Ahmedabad, Pearl Academy
   - Roles: Fashion Designer, Textile Designer, Stylist, Costume Designer
   - Salary: ₹3-8 LPA (starting), ₹15-50 LPA (experienced/own brand)

2. UX/UI DESIGN:
   - Education: B.Des, BFA, or even self-taught with strong portfolio
   - Top Colleges: IDC IIT Bombay, NID, Srishti Manipal
   - Roles: UX Designer, UI Designer, Product Designer, Design Researcher
   - Salary: ₹6-12 LPA (starting at top companies), ₹20-50 LPA (senior)

3. GRAPHIC & COMMUNICATION DESIGN:
   - Education: B.Des in Communication Design
   - Roles: Brand Designer, Art Director, Motion Graphics Artist
   - Growing sectors: EdTech, D2C brands, advertising agencies

INDUSTRY INSIGHT: India's design industry is booming. Companies like Swiggy, Zomato, CRED, and Razorpay are hiring designers at salaries comparable to software engineers.
clues.hint: Design is no longer considered a 'lesser' career in India. UX designers at top companies earn as much as software engineers. The key is the right institution and a killer portfolio.

clues.label: UX Case Study on the iMac
clues.content:
CASE STUDY: How Swiggy Redesigned Their Checkout Flow

PROBLEM: 34% of users were abandoning their cart at checkout.

RESEARCH: The UX team conducted user interviews and discovered:
- Users were confused by too many payment options shown at once
- The 'Apply Coupon' button was hard to find
- Users didn't trust the app because the order summary was hidden

SOLUTION:
- Simplified payment screen to show top 3 methods, with 'More Options' expandable
- Made coupon field prominent with auto-apply suggestions
- Added a persistent, transparent order summary

RESULT: Cart abandonment dropped from 34% to 18% -- a ₹200 crore annual revenue increase.

LESSON: UX design directly impacts business revenue. This is why companies invest heavily in design teams. A single design improvement can be worth crores.
clues.hint: This case study shows that UX design isn't just art -- it's a business skill that directly affects revenue. Good designers need both empathy for users AND understanding of business metrics.

puzzle.question: Meera is a Class 11 student who loves both art and technology. She wants a design career with strong job prospects and high earning potential. Based on the clues, what should be her PRIMARY strategy?
options: Skip college entirely since portfolios matter more than degrees -- just learn Photoshop and start freelancing immediately
Study pure fine arts (BFA) because all design is essentially art, and technical tools can be learned later
Prepare for NIFT/NID/UCEED entrance exams while simultaneously building a portfolio of real projects that demonstrate both design thinking and user problem-solving
Become a software engineer first and then switch to design later, since tech pays more
puzzle.correct_answer: Prepare for NIFT/NID/UCEED entrance exams while simultaneously building a portfolio of real projects that demonstrate both design thinking and user problem-solving
puzzle.success_message: Brilliant! You've escaped The Design Studio! Combining a strong institutional foundation (NIFT/NID) with a portfolio showing real problem-solving is the most effective path. Design is where creativity meets strategy! The Medical Wing awaits!
puzzle.fail_message: Not quite! The clues revealed that while portfolios are crucial, a top design institution provides the network, mentorship, and structured thinking that self-learning alone can't match. The best strategy combines both. Try again!

rooms.title: The Medical Wing
rooms.description: The smell of antiseptic fills the air. Anatomical charts cover the walls, a stethoscope hangs from a hook, and medical textbooks are stacked high. This is the world of healthcare and medicine. Explore what it truly means to pursue a career in healing!

clues.label: Anatomy & Medical Journey Chart
clues.content:
THE DOCTOR'S JOURNEY IN INDIA:

1. CLASS 11-12: PCB stream (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
2. ENTRANCE EXAM: NEET-UG (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test)
   - ~20 lakh students appear annually
   - ~1 lakh MBBS seats available (govt + private)
   - For AIIMS/top govt colleges: Need top 0.1% rank
3. MBBS: 5.5 years (4.5 years academic + 1 year internship)
4. SPECIALISATION (Optional but recommended):
   - NEET-PG for MD/MS (3 years)
   - Super-specialisation: DM/MCh (3 more years)

TOTAL TIME: 5.5 years (general doctor) to 11.5 years (super-specialist)

SPECIALISATION EXAMPLES:
- MD Medicine → DM Cardiology (Heart)
- MS Surgery → MCh Neurosurgery (Brain)
- MD Paediatrics → DM Neonatology (Newborns)

INCOME REALITY:
- Govt doctor (starting): ₹60,000-80,000/month
- Private practice (established): ₹3-15 LPA (GP) to ₹50 LPA-2 Cr+ (super-specialist surgeon)
clues.hint: Medicine is one of the longest educational journeys. Notice the time investment -- a super-specialist may be 30+ years old before they fully start their career. This requires serious commitment.

clues.label: Medical Ethics Handbook
clues.content:
MEDICAL ETHICS -- THE 4 PILLARS:

1. AUTONOMY: Respect the patient's right to make their own decisions
   - Example: A patient has the right to refuse treatment, even if the doctor disagrees

2. BENEFICENCE: Act in the patient's best interest
   - Example: Recommending the most effective treatment, not the most expensive one

3. NON-MALEFICENCE: 'First, do no harm' (Primum non nocere)
   - Example: Not prescribing unnecessary antibiotics that could cause resistance

4. JUSTICE: Treat all patients fairly regardless of background
   - Example: A government hospital doctor must give equal care to every patient

CASE STUDY: Dr. Aruna at a rural PHC (Primary Health Centre) in Jharkhand faces a dilemma -- she has limited medicine supplies and 50 patients waiting. She must TRIAGE -- prioritise based on medical urgency, not who came first or who can pay more. This is justice and beneficence in action.

REALITY CHECK: 60% of India's doctors serve the urban 40% of the population. Rural healthcare remains critically understaffed.
clues.hint: Ethics isn't a theoretical concept in medicine -- it's a daily practice. Doctors face impossible choices regularly. The 4 pillars help guide these decisions.

clues.label: Healthcare Careers Beyond MBBS
clues.content:
HEALTHCARE ISN'T JUST ABOUT BECOMING A DOCTOR!

ALLIED HEALTH CAREERS:
- Physiotherapist (BPT, 4.5 years): Helps patients recover movement after injuries
- Clinical Psychologist (BA/MA Psychology + MPhil): Treats mental health conditions
- Biomedical Engineer (B.Tech Biomedical): Designs medical devices like pacemakers, MRI machines
- Pharmacist (B.Pharm/D.Pharm): Develops and dispenses medicines
- Public Health Specialist (MBBS + MPH): Designs health policies for populations
- Medical Researcher (PhD): Discovers new treatments and drugs

GROWING FIELDS:
- Telemedicine: Remote consultations boomed post-COVID (Practo, Apollo 24/7)
- Healthcare AI: Using machine learning to read X-rays and predict diseases
- Genomics: Personalised medicine based on your DNA

INSTITUTIONS BEYOND AIIMS:
- CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry, Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC) Pune
- For allied health: Manipal Academy, SRM, MAHE
- For public health: IIPH, TISS, PHFI
clues.hint: If medicine interests you but MBBS feels too long or competitive, there are dozens of allied health careers that are equally meaningful and in high demand.

clues.label: Diagnostic Reasoning Case
clues.content:
DIAGNOSTIC REASONING EXERCISE:

Patient: 16-year-old student
Symptoms: Persistent fatigue, difficulty concentrating in class, frequent headaches, pale skin, craving for ice

Dr. Patel's approach:
1. HISTORY: Asked about diet -- patient is vegetarian and skips breakfast regularly
2. EXAMINATION: Pale conjunctiva (inner eyelid), spoon-shaped nails
3. INVESTIGATION: Ordered a Complete Blood Count (CBC)
4. RESULT: Haemoglobin = 8.2 g/dL (normal for teens: 12-16 g/dL)
5. DIAGNOSIS: Iron Deficiency Anaemia
6. TREATMENT: Iron supplements + dietary changes (spinach, jaggery, vitamin C for absorption)

KEY INSIGHT: Doctors don't just treat symptoms -- they investigate root causes. This patient didn't need a headache pill. They needed iron. DIAGNOSTIC REASONING is the core skill that separates a doctor from a Google search.

FUN FACT: Iron deficiency anaemia affects ~50% of Indian women and adolescent girls, making it a major public health concern.
clues.hint: This case shows the step-by-step diagnostic process doctors use. Notice how the doctor didn't just treat the headache -- they dug deeper to find the underlying cause.

puzzle.question: Ravi wants to work in healthcare and is passionate about helping people, but he struggles with the idea of spending 11+ years in education and finds the NEET competition overwhelming. Based on the clues, what is the BEST advice for him?
options: Give up on healthcare entirely -- if you can't crack NEET, there's no point pursuing this field
Just keep attempting NEET every year until he passes -- there are no other options in healthcare

Explore allied health careers like physiotherapy, biomedical engineering, or clinical psychology, which have shorter training periods and are in high demand, while still making a meaningful impact on patients' lives
Become a doctor in another country where exams are easier, then return to India to practise
puzzle.correct_answer: Explore allied health careers like physiotherapy, biomedical engineering, or clinical psychology, which have shorter training periods and are in high demand, while still making a meaningful impact on patients' lives
puzzle.success_message: Outstanding! You've navigated The Medical Wing! Healthcare is a vast ecosystem -- not just doctors. Physiotherapists, biomedical engineers, psychologists, and public health experts all save lives in different ways. One more room to go!
puzzle.fail_message: Not quite! The clues showed that healthcare extends far beyond MBBS. Allied health careers offer meaningful, high-demand alternatives with shorter training periods. The best career is one that matches your passion AND your practical situation. Try again!

rooms.title: The Entrepreneur's Office
rooms.description: A chaotic desk covered in sticky notes, pitch decks, and coffee cups. A whiteboard reads 'Launch Day: T-minus 30 days.' This is the world of business and startups. Discover what it takes to turn an idea into an empire!

clues.label: Business Plan Template on the Desk
clues.content:
THE LEAN BUSINESS PLAN -- ONE PAGE IS ENOUGH TO START:

1. PROBLEM: What pain point are you solving?
   Example: 'Students in Tier-2 cities lack access to quality career counselling'

2. SOLUTION: How do you solve it?
   Example: 'An AI-powered app that provides personalised career guidance in Hindi and English'

3. TARGET MARKET: Who are your customers?
   Example: 'Class 9-12 students in Tier-2/3 cities (approx. 80 million students)'

4. REVENUE MODEL: How do you make money?
   - Freemium (basic free, premium paid)
   - Subscription (monthly/yearly)
   - B2B (sell to schools)
   - Commission-based (partner with colleges)

5. UNFAIR ADVANTAGE: What makes you hard to copy?
   Example: 'Vernacular AI + partnerships with 500 schools'

STICKY NOTE: 'An idea without execution is just a daydream. Investors don't fund ideas -- they fund teams that can execute.'
clues.hint: A business plan doesn't need to be 100 pages. The best entrepreneurs can explain their entire business on one page. Clarity of thinking is the real skill.

clues.label: Startup Funding Stages Poster
clues.content:
STARTUP FUNDING STAGES IN INDIA:

1. BOOTSTRAPPING (Self-funded): ₹0-5 lakh
   - Use your own savings or family support
   - Build an MVP (Minimum Viable Product)
   - Example: Zerodha started with founders' savings

2. ANGEL INVESTMENT: ₹5-50 lakh
   - Individual investors who bet on early-stage ideas
   - Networks: Indian Angel Network, Mumbai Angels, LetsVenture

3. SEED ROUND: ₹50 lakh - ₹5 crore
   - VC firms fund startups with some traction
   - Key VCs: Blume Ventures, 100X.VC, Titan Capital (Snapdeal founder)

4. SERIES A/B/C: ₹5 crore - ₹500 crore+
   - Major VC firms for proven, scaling businesses
   - Key VCs: Sequoia Capital India, Accel, Tiger Global

5. IPO (Initial Public Offering):
   - Company goes public on stock exchange (BSE/NSE)
   - Examples: Zomato IPO (2021), Nykaa IPO (2021)

CRITICAL FACT: 90% of Indian startups fail within 5 years. Top reasons: no market need (42%), ran out of cash (29%), wrong team (23%).

GOVERNMENT SUPPORT: Startup India scheme offers tax benefits, easier compliance, and funding support for registered startups.
clues.hint: Notice the failure rate -- 90%! Entrepreneurship is high risk, high reward. Understanding funding stages helps you know when and how to raise money smartly.

clues.label: Market Research Report
clues.content:
MARKET RESEARCH: WHY MOST STARTUPS FAIL

CASE STUDY -- A TALE OF TWO STARTUPS:

STARTUP A (FAILED): 'GrocerFast'
- Founder's assumption: 'Everyone wants 10-minute grocery delivery in Jaipur'
- Spent ₹80 lakh building the app before talking to a single customer
- Launched to discover: Customers in Jaipur preferred calling their local kirana store
- Shut down in 6 months

STARTUP B (SUCCEEDED): 'KiranaConnect'
- Founder's approach: Spent 3 months interviewing 200 kirana store owners
- Discovered their real pain point: inventory management, not delivery
- Built a simple WhatsApp-based inventory tool (MVP cost: ₹2 lakh)
- Now serves 10,000 stores across Rajasthan

LESSON: Build what people NEED, not what you ASSUME they want.

MARKET RESEARCH METHODS:
- Customer interviews (talk to 50+ potential users)
- Surveys (Google Forms, Typeform)
- Competitor analysis (who else solves this problem?)
- Landing page test (build a fake product page, measure sign-ups)
- TAM/SAM/SOM analysis (Total, Serviceable, Obtainable Market size)
clues.hint: The difference between Startup A and Startup B is crystal clear: one assumed, the other researched. Market research isn't optional -- it's survival.

clues.label: Entrepreneur's Skillset Assessment
clues.content:
WHAT MAKES A SUCCESSFUL ENTREPRENEUR? (It's NOT just a great idea)

1. RESILIENCE: You WILL face rejection. Investors will say no. Customers will complain. Can you bounce back?
   - Byju Raveendran was rejected by multiple investors before building India's largest edtech company

2. FINANCIAL LITERACY: Understanding unit economics, burn rate, margins
   - If your customer acquisition cost (CAC) is ₹500 but each customer only pays ₹200, you LOSE money on every sale

3. SALESMANSHIP: You must sell -- to investors, customers, employees, partners
   - Even technical founders need to pitch their vision compellingly

4. ADAPTABILITY (PIVOTING): Your first idea will probably fail. Can you pivot?
   - Slack started as a gaming company before becoming a messaging tool
   - Instagram started as a location check-in app called Burbn

5. TEAM BUILDING: Solo founders have a 3x higher failure rate
   - Find a co-founder whose skills complement yours (tech + business, design + marketing)

ENTREPRENEURSHIP EDUCATION IN INDIA:
- MBA from IIM-A/B/C, ISB, XLRI
- Startup incubators: T-Hub Hyderabad, IIT Madras Incubation Cell, NSRCEL IIM Bangalore
- Competitions: Smart India Hackathon, Shark Tank India, E-Cell events at IITs
clues.hint: Notice that most entrepreneurial skills are about mindset and people skills, not technical knowledge. Resilience, sales, adaptability -- these are learnable skills, not innate talents.

puzzle.question: Ananya has a brilliant idea for an EdTech app targeting rural students. She has ₹3 lakh in savings and wants to launch as soon as possible. Based on the clues, what should be her FIRST step?
options: Spend the entire ₹3 lakh building a full-featured app with all the bells and whistles, then launch and hope for the best
Immediately pitch to Sequoia Capital for a Series A round of ₹10 crore to build the app properly
Conduct market research by interviewing 50+ rural students and teachers to validate the problem, then build a simple MVP to test with real users before scaling
Quit her current studies to focus full-time on the startup, because entrepreneurs need 100% commitment from day one
puzzle.correct_answer: Conduct market research by interviewing 50+ rural students and teachers to validate the problem, then build a simple MVP to test with real users before scaling
puzzle.success_message: You've escaped The Entrepreneur's Office and completed the Career Explorer! The GrocerFast vs KiranaConnect case study showed exactly why: validate first, build second. Talking to customers before spending money is the single most important startup lesson. Congratulations -- your future is unlocked!
puzzle.fail_message: Not quite! Remember the tale of GrocerFast vs KiranaConnect -- the startup that spent ₹80 lakh without talking to customers failed, while the one that researched first succeeded. Always validate your idea with real users before investing heavily. Try again!

glossary_terms.definition: The simplest version of a product that lets you test your core idea with real users. Instead of building everything, you build just enough to learn whether people actually want what you're offering. For example, a one-page website or a basic app with only the key feature.

The process of designing products (apps, websites, physical products) that are easy, enjoyable, and meaningful for people to use. UX designers research how users think and behave, then design interfaces that solve their problems intuitively. It combines psychology, design, and business thinking.

India's single national-level entrance exam for admission to MBBS, BDS, and other medical courses in government and private colleges across the country. Conducted by NTA (National Testing Agency), it tests Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. Over 20 lakh students appear for approximately 1 lakh seats annually.

The rate at which a startup spends money each month before becoming profitable. If a company earns ₹2 lakh per month but spends ₹5 lakh, its burn rate is ₹3 lakh/month. 'Runway' is how long the company can survive at the current burn rate before running out of cash.

A curated collection of your best work that demonstrates your skills, creativity, and process to potential employers or clients. Essential for careers in design, architecture, photography, writing, and increasingly in tech (via GitHub projects). Unlike a resume that lists credentials, a portfolio SHOWS what you can actually do.
